claim: GSAM states its Liquidity Solutions team oversees more than $1.2 trillion in money market and short-term assets.
passage: Our Liquidity Solutions team oversees $1.2+ trillion in money market and short-term assets.
notes: Assets under supervision, which include assets where GS lacks full discretion. Global figure, not EMEA. Not fee-earning AUM and not revenue.

claim: GSAM says Liquidity Solutions works with financial institution, hedge fund, institutional, corporate and wealth management clients.
passage: financial institution, hedge fund, institutional, corporate, and wealth management clients
notes: Client list is by type, not by region. Liquidity is a product line that cuts across client segments.

claim: The UK institutional page lists GS US$ Liquid Reserves Fund and GS Euro Liquid Reserves Fund as LVNAV money market funds and GS US$ Treasury Liquid Reserves Fund as a Public Debt CNAV fund, alongside short-duration strategies, fixed income ETFs and the Mosaic portal.
passage: Product table: LVNAV (Low Volatility NAV); Public Debt CNAV (Constant NAV); Mosaic 'allows clients to seamlessly manage investments, reporting and risk across their liquidity portfolio'
notes: The page did not show a sterling fund or a named VNAV fund in the extract read; the wider range (sterling, yen, standard VNAV) was not verified here. Fund legal structure and domicile (Irish umbrella) not read in this research.

claim: Liquidity Solutions has global, not regional, leadership: a Global Head of Insurance Asset Management and Liquidity Solutions and a separate Global Head of Liquidity Solutions Client Business are named on the product page.
passage: Mike Siegel: Global Head, Insurance Asset Management and Liquidity Solutions; Frank Murphy: Global Head, Liquidity Solutions Client Business
notes: Supports treating Liquidity Solutions as a global product-line client business rather than a regional coverage team. Reporting lines inside EMEA not established.

claim: A London job ad describes an 'EMEA Liquidity Solutions' sales channel serving treasury teams at corporations, hedge funds, private equity, VCs and public institutions, with a role dedicated to UK corporate and insurance clients.
passage: EMEA Liquidity Solutions Sales Team (UK Corporates)... treasury teams at Corporations, Hedge Funds, Private Equity, VCs and Public Institutions of all sizes
notes: Known from search-result fragments; ad page not read in full. Suggests the EMEA liquidity team is itself split by client type and country (a 'UK Corporates' seat implies other seats). Internal split otherwise not established.

claim: No public evidence was found that French is required for Liquidity Solutions roles; the one French-speaker ad found belongs to the 'EMEA French Sales Team' covering third-party wealth clients, and the UK Corporates liquidity ad showed no language requirement in the text seen.
passage: Reference: search summaries of both ads; neither full text was read.
notes: The former intern's remark that everyone in Liquidity Solutions speaks French remains an Unverified account. A plausible but unproven explanation is that some EMEA liquidity seats cover French-speaking corporates. Searched but not established.

claim: A money market fund investor earns the portfolio's yield net of the fund's ongoing charge; the manager's revenue is that charge on average balances, which is thin per unit of assets and can be waived when yields are very low.
passage: Reference: general fund mechanics; the GS page states funds aim to 'maximise current income' consistent with capital preservation and liquidity.
notes: Interpretation, not a GS disclosure. No GS fee rate or waiver figure was read in this research; do not quote one. Fee-waiver history sits in GS annual filings (see stream R2).

claim: The FCA said on 8 June 2026 that the Government expects to repeal the UK MMF Regulation by end-2026, with FCA rules to the same timetable and guidance expecting stable-NAV MMFs to hold 40% weekly liquid assets and VNAV MMFs 20%.
passage: expects, through guidance, that stable NAV MMFs hold 40% and variable NAV MMFs hold 20%
notes: Earlier CP23/28 proposals (15% daily / 50% weekly) were softened. Final rules had not been read as published at the cutoff. Applies to UK-domiciled MMFs; most sterling MMF assets are in EU-domiciled funds.

claim: EU-domiciled money market funds, which hold roughly 90% of sterling MMF assets, are sold in the UK under a temporary permissions regime that is being extended while an equivalence decision is pending.
passage: EU-domiciled MMFs account for about 90% of sterling MMF assets under management
notes: Law-firm commentary; the end date (end-2027) and equivalence timing (2027) are indicative. Matters because GS's European liquidity funds are EU funds marketed to UK treasurers (fund domicile not verified here).

claim: The European Commission's 2026 follow-up report recommended no significant legislative reform of the EU MMF Regulation and referred to 40% (stable NAV) and 20% (VNAV) weekly liquidity as supervisory benchmarks.
passage: supervisory and risk-management benchmarks rather than new binding regulatory minima
notes: Read via a law-firm summary, not the Commission document itself.

claim: In July 2025 BNY and Goldman Sachs launched a solution that mirrors money market fund shares as tokens on Goldman's GS DAP ledger, with BNY remaining the official record; GSAM was among the initial fund managers.
passage: Reference: GS/BNY press release title and search-result summary; page returned HTTP 403.
notes: Launch-era, US-focused coverage. No evidence on volumes, or on availability for European funds or EMEA clients. Stated aim is collateral mobility, not a new product for treasurers yet.

claim: GSAM states it manages $651 billion in general account assets on behalf of insurance clients.
passage: manages $651 billion in general account assets on behalf of insurance clients
notes: Global figure; includes the NN Group partnership assets by implication but the split is not disclosed. General-account assets only.

claim: The 15th annual GSAM Global Insurance Survey (published 25 March 2026) polled 434 insurance CIOs and CFOs between 11 January and 3 February 2026; 62% plan to increase private asset allocations and asset-backed finance had the highest net intended increase (38%).
passage: 434 senior investment professionals... 62% plan to increase private asset allocations this year
notes: Stated intentions, not actual flows. No EMEA breakdown on the pages read. 55% expect a US recession within three years (46% a year earlier).

claim: Insurance is run as a global client vertical: GSAM names a Global Head of Insurance Asset Management and Liquidity Solutions and a Global Head of the Insurance Asset Management business, and advertises 'Insurance Client Solutions Group' roles in London and Frankfurt.
passage: Mike Siegel, Global Head of Insurance Asset Management and Liquidity Solutions, Co-Head of the Client Solutions Group in Asia Pacific
notes: Titles verified on the press release; the London and Frankfurt job titles come from search listings. Whether the EMEA insurance team reports regionally, globally or both is not publicly established. Answers the 'where does Insurance sit' question only partly.

claim: GSAM describes its insurance offer as partial to full outsourcing across fixed income, alternatives and equities, plus advisory on asset-liability management, strategic asset allocation, capital-efficient strategies and risk management.
passage: partial to full outsourcing solutions involving fixed-income strategies... asset liability management, strategic asset allocation, capital-efficient investment strategies
notes: Marketing description. Shows why insurance coverage needs specialists: the product is a balance-sheet service, not a single fund.

claim: A Frankfurt Insurance Client Solutions Group ad says the Insurance Asset Management team provides solutions for life, health, property and casualty and reinsurance companies, with associates supporting the relationship management team.
passage: provides solutions for life, health, property and casualty and reinsurance companies
notes: Search-result fragment; full ad not read.

claim: Goldman Sachs completed the acquisition of NN Investment Partners in April 2022 for about EUR 1.7 billion; reporting at the time said it took European AUS above $600 billion and extended the firm's insurance asset management business.
passage: European AUS exceed US$600 billion... extends Goldman's leadership in insurance asset management
notes: 2022 figures, not current. Trade-press report of the completion announcement.

claim: On completion GSAM entered a long-term strategic partnership with NN Group to manage an approximately $180 billion portfolio, and more than 900 NN IP employees joined.
passage: long-term strategic partnership agreement with NN Group to manage an approximately $180 billion portfolio
notes: Search-result summary. A ten-year term appears in earlier drafts but was not confirmed in any page read; treat the duration as not established here. The Hague as the Dutch base was also not confirmed in a page read (a GS job title 'CCG Analyst - The Hague' is consistent with it).

claim: Amended EU Solvency II rules (Directive (EU) 2025/2) take effect on 30 January 2027.
passage: The new rules take effect on 30 January 2027
notes: The specific changes (risk margin, long-term equity treatment) were not on the page read; do not quote details without the directive text.

claim: The PRA consulted in April 2025 on a Matching Adjustment Investment Accelerator letting insurers add self-assessed eligible assets to matching-adjustment portfolios before approval, within a limit of the lower of 5% of MA best-estimate liabilities or GBP 2 billion and a 24-month regularisation window.
passage: 24 months to submit an MA application to regularise those assets
notes: This is the consultation. The final policy statement and its effective date were not read in this research (searched but not established); confirm before quoting as in force.

claim: Goldman Sachs advertised in October 2026 a London-based Client Solutions Group analyst/associate role supporting the BeNeLux Institutional Sales Team, with native Dutch essential and French an advantage.
passage: Native Dutch speaker is essential (written and oral fluency) with French an advantage
notes: Read on a job-board mirror of the GS ad. The team is described as responsible for new business development and existing institutional client relationships, i.e. sales and relationship management together. Confirms the intern's point that Benelux needs a local language.

claim: Benelux third-party wealth sales roles are advertised in The Hague or Amsterdam (Dutch and English) and Brussels (French, English and Dutch), and a 'CCG Analyst' role is titled for The Hague.
passage: Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management - CCG Analyst - The Hague
notes: Search listings only. Indicates Benelux coverage is split between local offices and London-based support, and that 'CCG' is used in public job titles.

claim: In May 2020 GSAM merged third-party distribution and institutional sales into one Nordic organisation selling all asset classes to all client types across the Nordic countries, with offices in Stockholm, Copenhagen and London.
passage: Reference: Realtid, 13 May 2020 (Swedish; translated).
notes: Historical. Whether the same structure and leadership hold at November 2026 was not confirmed. It shows a region need not be split into separate TPW and Institutional teams the way the UK reportedly is.

claim: A London-based Nordics Institutional Sales Support Analyst ad requires native Swedish and describes the Nordics team as handling new business and client relationships with pension funds and sovereign wealth funds.
passage: Reference: search-result summary of higher.gs.com role 146152; page not readable.
notes: Confirms in direction the intern's claim that Nordics needs a local language. Date and live status not confirmed.

claim: CSG student and TPW roles are advertised in Stockholm and Copenhagen (2027 Stockholm off-cycle analyst; Copenhagen Nordic TPW client coverage).
passage: 2027 | EMEA | Stockholm | Asset Management, Client Solutions Group | Seasonal/Off-Cycle Analyst
notes: Titles from search listings.

claim: GSAM has a 'TPW Switzerland team' with a dedicated head since January 2025, and has advertised a London-based sales support analyst for the Swiss client base.
passage: We are seeking to hire a Sales Support Analyst to join our TPW Switzerland team.
notes: The London ad mirror listed no language requirement, while a Zurich TPW alternatives ad (search summary) requires German. Swiss institutional coverage (pension funds) was not found: searched but not established.

claim: Evidence on language for Swiss coverage is mixed: a Zurich third-party wealth role requires German with other European languages preferred, but a London-based Swiss sales-support ad listed no language requirement on the mirror read.
passage: German is required, and European languages preferable (Italian, French, Spanish)
notes: The intern said Switzerland needs a local language. Likely true for client-facing seats; not shown for every support seat.

claim: Germany and Austria are covered by a Frankfurt-based client business: public ads refer to the 'Institutional Sales Team for Germany & Austria', a 'German TPW team' requiring native German, an Insurance Client Solutions Group seat and CSG analyst hiring in Frankfurt.
passage: our German TPW team... Native German and English speaker is essential (written and oral fluency)
notes: German TPW ad verified on a mirror; others from search listings. A head of client business for Germany and Austria existed in 2021 (verified, historical). This answers the intern's gap: Germany is covered locally, not from the London teams he listed.

claim: France appears to be covered by a French sales team with seats in both Paris and London: a 2027 Paris off-cycle CSG role sits in a Third Party Wealth sub-team for French speakers, and a London sales-support role in the 'EMEA French Sales Team' requires fluent French.
passage: Reference: search-result summaries; ad pages not readable.
notes: No ad text was read directly. French institutional coverage not established.

claim: Italy is covered from Milan: public listings show a 2027 Milan CSG off-cycle analyst role and a Milan Third Party Wealth sales associate role, and 2025 reporting describes Goldman's Italian third-party wealth relationships with private banks, asset managers and insurers.
passage: 2027 | EMEA | Milan | Asset Management, Client Solutions Group | Seasonal/Off-Cycle Analyst
notes: Titles and a news summary from search listings.

claim: GSAM runs a Spanish-language site with a Spanish sales service line and Goldman Sachs has a Madrid office, but no public source read here establishes a Madrid-based GSAM Client Solutions team or its structure.
passage: Servicio de atencion para ventas
notes: Not yet fully investigated: the shared search budget ran out before Iberia-specific searches. The Madrid office evidence is from the private wealth site.

claim: Goldman Sachs has offices in Dubai, Doha and Riyadh, announced an Abu Dhabi Global Market office in 2023, opened a Kuwait office in October 2025 and officially opened a Riyadh regional headquarters in KAFD in December 2025.
passage: opening 'a new office in Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM)'... new office in Kuwait, opened in October 2025
notes: Firm-level offices. Which of them house GSAM client-coverage staff is not stated. The KAFD release names asset and wealth management among Saudi businesses.

claim: A 2027 Dubai-based 'Asset Management, Client Solutions Group' seasonal/off-cycle role is listed, so at least part of Middle East asset-management client coverage sits in Dubai.
passage: 2027 | EMEA | Dubai | Asset Management, Client Solutions Group | Seasonal/Off-Cycle
notes: Title only. Does not show how coverage is divided between Dubai and London, and no public source confirmed the intern's account that a London Middle East team hires summer analysts.

claim: Whether Arabic is required for Middle East coverage, and whether the Middle East team is split into Third Party Wealth and Institutional, could not be established from public sources.
passage: Reference: no Middle East client-coverage job text was readable.
notes: Both remain the former intern's Unverified account. Searched (job-ad searches for Middle East CSG roles) but not established.

claim: In February 2024 Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Mubadala signed a US$1 billion separately managed account to co-invest in Asia Pacific private credit.
passage: separately managed account... U$1bn of long-term capital
notes: A commitment to a partnership vehicle, not funded fee-paying assets on day one. Managed by Private Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives; no public attribution to a Middle East client-coverage team.

claim: A Goldman Sachs job ad describes a Client Solutions Group role working with 'institutional, third-party wealth, insurance and consultant relations teams', consistent with insurance being a peer channel to institutional and third-party wealth.
passage: Reference: search-result summary; ad page returned HTTP 403.
notes: Supports Layer B reading that CSG is cut by client channel as well as by region.

claim: Across EMEA, public job ads show the Client Solutions Group organised as a matrix: country or region teams (Benelux, Nordics, Germany/Austria, France, Italy, Switzerland) crossed with channel (Institutional, Third Party Wealth, Insurance, Liquidity), with some sales-support seats in London and client-facing seats in local offices.
passage: Reference: pattern across the cited job ads.
notes: Interpretation from job ads, not an org chart. No reporting lines are established. It contradicts a strict reading of the intern's 'six teams' list: continental teams exist beyond those he named, mostly based outside London.

claim: Every continental coverage ad read or summarised required a local language (Dutch, Swedish, German, French), which supports in direction the intern's view that an English-only candidate is most plausible for UK-focused seats.
passage: Native Dutch speaker is essential... Native German and English speaker is essential
notes: A sample of ads, not a policy. No Middle East or Liquidity ad text confirming 'English only' was read.

claim: Thirty Dutch pension funds holding about EUR 542 billion had converted to the new pension system by 31 March 2026, and funds have until 1 January 2028 to transfer accrued entitlements.
passage: Pension funds have until 1 January 2028 to transfer accrued pension entitlements.
notes: 24 of the 30 moved on 1 January 2026.

claim: Commentary from a competing LDI manager says rates markets stayed calm around the January 2026 transition and expects larger hedge reductions in January 2027, with insurers buying long duration.
passage: the feared dislocations failed to materialise
notes: One manager's opinion and estimates. Use as an example of the debate, not as fact about future flows.
